Remarks on the global regularity of two-dimensional magnetohydrodynamics system with zero dissipationThanks: The author expresses gratitude to Professor Jiahong Wu for suggesting this direction of research and Professor David Ullrich for his teaching. The author also expresses gratitude to the referees for helpful suggestions.

Kazuo Yamazaki
Abstract.

We study the two-dimensional magnetohydrodynamics system with generalized dissipation and diffusion in terms of fractional Laplacians. It is known that the classical magnetohydrodynamics system with full Laplacians in both dissipation and diffusion terms admits a unique global strong solution pair. Making use of the special structure of the system in the two-dimensional case, we show in particular that the solution pair remains smooth when we have zero dissipation but only magnetic diffusion with its power of the fractional Laplacian β>32\beta>\frac{3}{2}.

Keywords: Global regularity, magnetohydrodynamics system, Navier-Stokes system, Euler equations, Littlewood-Paley theory

11 1 2000MSC : 35B65, 35Q35, 35Q8622 2 Department of Mathematics, Oklahoma State University, 401 Mathematical Sciences, Stillwater, OK 74078, USA

1. Introduction and statement of results

We study the following magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) system:

{∂u∂t+(u⋅∇)u−(b⋅∇)b+∇π+νΛ2​αu=0∂b∂t+(u⋅∇)b−(b⋅∇)u+ηΛ2​βb=0∇⋅u=∇⋅b=0,(u,b)​(x,0)=(u0,b0)​(x)\begin{cases}\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}+(u\cdot\nabla)u-(b\cdot\nabla)b+\nabla\pi+\nu\Lambda^{2\alpha}u=0\\ \frac{\partial b}{\partial t}+(u\cdot\nabla)b-(b\cdot\nabla)u+\eta\Lambda^{2\beta}b=0\\ \nabla\cdot u=\nabla\cdot b=0,\hskip 8.53581pt(u,b)(x,0)=(u_{0},b_{0})(x)\end{cases} (1)

where u:ℝN×ℝ+↦ℝNu:\mathbb{R}^{N}\times\mathbb{R}^{+}\mapsto\mathbb{R}^{N} represents the velocity vector field, b:ℝN×ℝ+↦ℝNb:\mathbb{R}^{N}\times\mathbb{R}^{+}\mapsto\mathbb{R}^{N} the magnetic vector field, π:ℝN×ℝ+↦ℝ\pi:\mathbb{R}^{N}\times\mathbb{R}^{+}\mapsto\mathbb{R} the pressure scalar field and ν,η≥0\nu,\eta\geq 0 are the kinematic viscosity and diffusivity constants respectively. We also let f^​(ξ)\hat{f}(\xi) denote the Fourier transform of ff; i.e.

f^(ξ)=∫ℝNf(x)e−ix⋅ξdx\hat{f}(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{N}}f(x)e^{-ix\cdot\xi}dx

and defined a fractional Laplacian operator Λ2​γ\Lambda^{2\gamma} with γ∈ℝ\gamma\in\mathbb{R} to have the Fourier symbol of |ξ|2​γ\lvert\xi\rvert^{2\gamma}; that is,

Λ2​γ​f^​(ξ)=|ξ|2​γ​f^​(ξ)\widehat{\Lambda^{2\gamma}f}(\xi)=\lvert\xi\rvert^{2\gamma}\hat{f}(\xi)

In case N=2,3,ν,η>0,α=β=1N=2,3,\nu,\eta>0,\alpha=\beta=1, the MHD system possesses at least one global L2L^{2} weak solution for any initial data pair (u0,b0)∈L2​(ℝN)×L2​(ℝN)(u_{0},b_{0})\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})\times L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N}); in case N=2N=2, in fact the solution is unique (cf. [20]).

In order to discuss the previous results on strong solutions and better understand the importance of the lower bounds for the two parameters α,β>0\alpha,\beta>0 when ν,η>0\nu,\eta>0, let us recall the notion of criticality in a simple setting. Firstly, it can be shown that the solution pair to (1) with α=β=γ\alpha=\beta=\gamma has the rescaling properties that if (u⁡(x,t),b⁡(x,t))(u(x,t),b(x,t)) solves the system, then so does (uλ​(x,t),bλ​(x,t))\left(u_{\lambda}(x,t),b_{\lambda}(x,t)\right) with λ∈ℝ+\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^{+} where

uλ​(x,t)=λ2​γ−1​u​(λ​x,λ2​γ​t),bλ​(x,t)=λ2​γ−1​b​(λ​x,λ2​γ​t),γ∈ℝ+u_{\lambda}(x,t)=\lambda^{2\gamma-1}u(\lambda x,\lambda^{2\gamma}t),\hskip 8.53581ptb_{\lambda}(x,t)=\lambda^{2\gamma-1}b(\lambda x,\lambda^{2\gamma}t),\hskip 8.53581pt\gamma\in\mathbb{R}^{+}

As we show in (4), the solution pair (u,b)(u,b) to (1) has the global bounds on the L2L^{2}-norm and it can be shown that γ=12+N4\gamma=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{N}{4} implies

∥uλ​(⋅,t)∥L2​(ℝN)=∥u⁡(⋅,λ2​γ​t)∥L2​(ℝN),∥bλ​(⋅,t)∥L2​(ℝN)=∥b⁡(⋅,λ2​γ​t)∥L2​(ℝN)\lVert u_{\lambda}(\cdot,t)\rVert_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}=\lVert u(\cdot,\lambda^{2\gamma}t)\rVert_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})},\hskip 8.53581pt\lVert b_{\lambda}(\cdot,t)\rVert_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}=\lVert b(\cdot,\lambda^{2\gamma}t)\rVert_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}

With this in mind, we call the case ν,η>0,α≥12+N4,β≥12+N4\nu,\eta>0,\alpha\geq\frac{1}{2}+\frac{N}{4},\beta\geq\frac{1}{2}+\frac{N}{4} the critical case and in such a case, the existence of the unique global strong solution pair has been shown (cf. [25]).

Some numerical analysis results (e.g. [11], [19]) indicate more dominant role played by the velocity vector field in preserving the regularity of the solution pair. Moreover, starting from the works of [12] and [31], we have also seen various regularity criteria of the MHD system in terms of only the velocity vector field (e.g. [2], [6], [8], [10], [13], [24], [27], [30]). This is largely due to the fact that upon taking H1H^{1}-estimates of uu and bb, every non-linear term involves uu while not necessarily bb. With this in mind, following the work of [21], the author in [23] showed that even in logarithmically super-critical case the system (1) still admits a unique global strong solution pair. That is, the author replaced the dissipative term of ν​Λ2​α​u\nu\Lambda^{2\alpha}u and the diffusive term of η​Λ2​β​b\eta\Lambda^{2\beta}b by ν​ℒ12​u\nu\mathcal{L}_{1}^{2}u and η​ℒ22​b\eta\mathcal{L}_{2}^{2}b respectively where ℒi,i=1,2\mathcal{L}_{i},i=1,2 are defined to have the Fourier symbols of mi​(ξ),i=1,2m_{i}(\xi),i=1,2 satisfying the following lower bounds:

ℒ1​u^​(ξ)=m1​(ξ)​u^​(ξ),ℒ2​b^​(ξ)=m2​(ξ)​b^​(ξ)\widehat{\mathcal{L}_{1}u}(\xi)=m_{1}(\xi)\hat{u}(\xi),\hskip 8.53581pt\widehat{\mathcal{L}_{2}b}(\xi)=m_{2}(\xi)\hat{b}(\xi)

and

m1​(ξ)≥|ξ|αg1​(ξ),m2​(ξ)≥|ξ|βg2​(ξ),α≥12+N4,β>0,α+β≥1+N2m_{1}(\xi)\geq\frac{\lvert\xi\rvert^{\alpha}}{g_{1}(\xi)},\hskip 8.53581ptm_{2}(\xi)\geq\frac{\lvert\xi\rvert^{\beta}}{g_{2}(\xi)},\hskip 8.53581pt\alpha\geq\frac{1}{2}+\frac{N}{4},\beta>0,\alpha+\beta\geq 1+\frac{N}{2}

with gi≥1,i=1,2g_{i}\geq 1,i=1,2 being radially symmetric, non-decreasing functions.

The endpoint case ν>0,η=0,α=1+N2\nu>0,\eta=0,\alpha=1+\frac{N}{2} was also completed recently in [28] (cf. also [26] for further generalization).

On the other hand, in case N=2N=2, it is well-known that the Euler equation, the Navier-Stokes system with no dissipation, admits a unique global strong solution. This is due to the fact that upon taking a curl, the vorticity becomes a conserved quantity. In the case of the MHD system, upon taking a curl and L2L^{2}-estimate of the resulting system, every non-linear term has bb involved. Exploiting this observation and divergence-free conditions, the authors in [3] showed that in case N=2N=2, full Laplacians in both dissipation and magnetic diffusion are not necessary for the solution to remain smooth; rather, only a mix of partial dissipation and diffusion in the order of two derivatives suffices. In this paper we make further observation in case N=2N=2:

Theorem 1.1.

Let N=2,ν=0,η>0,α=0,β>32N=2,\nu=0,\eta>0,\alpha=0,\beta>\frac{3}{2}. Then for all initial data pair (u0,b0)∈Hs​(ℝ2)×Hs​(ℝ2),s≥1+2​β(u_{0},b_{0})\in H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2})\times H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2}),s\geq 1+2\beta, there exists a unique global strong solution pair (u,b)(u,b) to (1) such that

u∈C⁡([0,∞),Hs​(ℝ2))\displaystyle u\in C([0,\infty);H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2}))
b∈C⁡([0,∞),Hs​(ℝ2))∩L2​([0,∞),Hs+β​(ℝ2))\displaystyle b\in C([0,\infty);H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2}))\cap L^{2}([0,\infty);H^{s+\beta}(\mathbb{R}^{2}))
Theorem 1.2.

Let N=2,ν,η>0,α∈(0,12),β∈(54,32]N=2,\nu,\eta>0,\alpha\in\left(0,\frac{1}{2}\right),\beta\in\left(\frac{5}{4},\frac{3}{2}\right] such that α+2​β>3\alpha+2\beta>3. Then for all initial data pair (u0,b0)∈Hs​(ℝ2)×Hs​(ℝ2),s≥1+2​β(u_{0},b_{0})\in H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2})\times H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2}),s\geq 1+2\beta, there exists a unique global strong solution pair (u,b)(u,b) to (1) such that

u∈C⁡([0,∞),Hs​(ℝ2))∩L2​([0,∞),Hs+α​(ℝ2))\displaystyle u\in C([0,\infty);H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2}))\cap L^{2}([0,\infty);H^{s+\alpha}(\mathbb{R}^{2}))
b∈C⁡([0,∞),Hs​(ℝ2))∩L2​([0,∞),Hs+β​(ℝ2))\displaystyle b\in C([0,\infty);H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2}))\cap L^{2}([0,\infty);H^{s+\beta}(\mathbb{R}^{2}))
Remark 1.1.
  1. (1)

    Our proof was inspired partially from the work of [3], [4] and [6]. We note that making use of the structure of the partial differential equation has proven to be useful in other cases as well (e.g. [29]).

  2. (2)

    While this paper was being prepared, the work by [22] appeared. In their work, it is shown that in particular if α=0\alpha=0, then β>2\beta>2 is required (See Theorem 1 and Remark 1 of [22]) while our Theorem 1.1 shows that β>32\beta>\frac{3}{2} suffices. We also independently obtained Theorem 5.1; this is no longer a new result and thus we placed this in the Appendix because its proof is immediate and very simple. The hypothesis of Theorem 5.1 allows α≥12\alpha\geq\frac{1}{2} rather than α=0\alpha=0 as in Theorem 1.1. As will be discussed, a complete lack of dissipation makes the analysis significantly more difficult in the latter case.

  3. (3)

    There are ways to obtain different initial regularity in various space of functions; we chose to state the above for simplicity. We also refer readers to [3] where the authors considered the case N=2,ν=0,η>0,β=1N=2,\nu=0,\eta>0,\beta=1 and showed the existence of weak solution pair and regularity criteria for its global regularity and uniqueness (cf. also [25]).

  4. (4)

    To extend such a type of result to higher dimension, it seems to require a new idea. As indicated in the work of [23] and [28], in higher dimension, dissipation seems to be crucial in preserving the regularity of the solution pair.

In the Preliminary section, let us briefly set up notations and state key lemmas; thereafter, we prove our theorems.

Next, we first obtain a higher regularity in the magnetic field only making use of diffusivity as much as possible:

Proposition 3.2.

Let N=2,ν=0,η>0,α=0,β>32N=2,\nu=0,\eta>0,\alpha=0,\beta>\frac{3}{2}. Then for any solution pair (u,b)(u,b) to (1) in [0,T][0,T], there exists a constant c⁡(u0,b0,T)>0c(u_{0},b_{0},T)>0 such that

supt∈[0,T]∥Λβ​b​(t)∥L22+η​∫0T∥Λ2​β​b∥L22​𝑑τ≤c⁡(u0,b0,T)\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}b(t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\eta\int_{0}^{T}\lVert\Lambda^{2\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}d\tau\leq c(u_{0},b_{0},T)
Proof.

Applying Λβ\Lambda^{\beta} on the second equation of (3) and taking L2L^{2}-inner products with Λβ​b\Lambda^{\beta}b, we have

12∂t∥Λβb∥L22+η∥Λ2​βb∥L22=−∫(u⋅∇)b⋅Λ2​βb+∫(b⋅∇)u⋅Λ2​βb\frac{1}{2}\partial_{t}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\eta\lVert\Lambda^{2\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}=-\int(u\cdot\nabla)b\cdot\Lambda^{2\beta}b+\int(b\cdot\nabla)u\cdot\Lambda^{2\beta}b

We bound the right hand side by

∥u∥L2​∥∇b∥L∞​∥Λ2​β​b∥L2+∥b∥L∞​∥∇u∥L2​∥Λ2​β​b∥L2\displaystyle\lVert u\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert\nabla b\rVert_{L^{\infty}}\lVert\Lambda^{2\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}+\lVert b\rVert_{L^{\infty}}\lVert\nabla u\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert\Lambda^{2\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}
≤\displaystyle\leq c⁡(∥Λ​b∥L2β−1β​∥Λ1+β​b∥L21β​∥Λ2​β​b∥L2+∥b∥L2β−1β​∥Λβ​b∥L21β​∥w∥L2​∥Λ2​β​b∥L2)\displaystyle c(\lVert\Lambda b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{\beta-1}{\beta}}\lVert\Lambda^{1+\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1}{\beta}}\lVert\Lambda^{2\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}+\lVert b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{\beta-1}{\beta}}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1}{\beta}}\lVert w\rVert_{L^{2}}\lVert\Lambda^{2\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}})

due to Ho¨\ddot{o}lder’s inequalities,

supt∈[0,T]∥u⁡(t)∥L2≤c⁡(u0,b0,T)\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\lVert u(t)\rVert_{L^{2}}\leq c(u_{0},b_{0},T)

from (4), Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequalities of

∥f∥L∞≤c0​∥f∥L2β−1β​∥Λβ​f∥L21β\lVert f\rVert_{L^{\infty}}\leq c_{0}\lVert f\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{\beta-1}{\beta}}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}f\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1}{\beta}} (7)

for some constant c0>0c_{0}>0 independent of ff and Lemma 2.1. Next, the bound on ∥b∥L2\lVert b\rVert_{L^{2}} from (4), the bound on ∥w∥L2\lVert w\rVert_{L^{2}} and ∥j∥L2\lVert j\rVert_{L^{2}} from Proposition 3.1 and Young’s inequalities lead to a further bound of

c⁡(∥Λ1+β​b∥L21β​∥Λ2​β​b∥L2+∥Λβ​b∥L21β​∥Λ2​β​b∥L2)≤η2​∥Λ2​β​b∥L22+c⁡(∥Λ1+β​b∥L22β+∥Λβ​b∥L22β)\displaystyle c(\lVert\Lambda^{1+\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1}{\beta}}\lVert\Lambda^{2\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}+\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1}{\beta}}\lVert\Lambda^{2\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}})\leq\frac{\eta}{2}\lVert\Lambda^{2\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+c(\lVert\Lambda^{1+\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{2}{\beta}}+\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{2}{\beta}})

We use this estimate, absorb the diffusive term, rely on Young’s inequality and integrate in time to obtain

supt∈[0,T]∥Λβ​b​(t)∥L22+η​∫0T∥Λ2​β​b∥L22​𝑑τ≤∥Λβ​b0∥L22+c​∫0T∥Λβ​j∥L22+∥Λβ​b∥L22+1​𝑑τ\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}b(t)\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\eta\int_{0}^{T}\lVert\Lambda^{2\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}d\tau\leq\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}b_{0}\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+c\int_{0}^{T}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}j\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{2}+1d\tau

According to (4) and Proposition 3.1, the time integral on the right hand side is bounded by some constant c⁡(u0,b0,T)c(u_{0},b_{0},T). This completes the proof of Proposition 3.2.

The higher regularity of the magnetic field from Proposition 3.2 allows us to prove the following proposition:

Proposition 3.3.

Let N=2,ν=0,η>0,α=0,β>32N=2,\nu=0,\eta>0,\alpha=0,\beta>\frac{3}{2}. Then for any solution pair (u,b)(u,b) to (1) in [0,T][0,T], there exists a constant c⁡(u0,b0,T)>0c(u_{0},b_{0},T)>0 such that

supt∈[0,T]∥w⁡(t)∥L∞≤c⁡(u0,b0,T)\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\lVert w(t)\rVert_{L^{\infty}}\leq c(u_{0},b_{0},T)

≤\displaystyle\leq c⁡(p)​c​∥b∥L22+p⁡(β−1)β​p​∥Λβ​b∥L21−2+p⁡(β−1)β​p​∥Λβ​b∥L22​β−3β​∥Λ2​β​b∥L23−ββ\displaystyle c(p)c\lVert b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{2+p(\beta-1)}{\beta p}}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{1-\frac{2+p(\beta-1)}{\beta p}}\lVert\Lambda^{\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{2\beta-3}{\beta}}\lVert\Lambda^{2\beta}b\rVert_{L^{2}}^{\frac{3-\beta}{\beta}}

We work on

The first proposition can be obtained similarly as before:

Proposition 4.1.

Let N=2,ν,η>0,α∈(0,12),β∈(54,32]N=2,\nu,\eta>0,\alpha\in(0,\frac{1}{2}),\beta\in(\frac{5}{4},\frac{3}{2}] such that α+2​β>3\alpha+2\beta>3. Then for any solution pair (u,b)(u,b) to (1) in [0,T][0,T], there exists a constant c⁡(u0,b0,T)>0c(u_{0},b_{0},T)>0 such that

by Ho¨\ddot{o}lder’s and Young’s inequalities. Now we estimate separately. By Lemma 2.5, we have

5.3. Proof of Lemma 2.3

We fix s>2s>2 and estimate

∥∇f∥L∞\displaystyle\lVert\nabla f\rVert_{L^{\infty}} ≤\displaystyle\leq c(∥f∥L2+∑j=0n−1∥Δj∇f∥L∞+∑j=n∞∥Δj∇f∥L∞)\displaystyle c(\lVert f\rVert_{L^{2}}+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\lVert\Delta_{j}\nabla f\rVert_{L^{\infty}}+\sum_{j=n}^{\infty}\lVert\Delta_{j}\nabla f\rVert_{L^{\infty}})
≤\displaystyle\leq c(∥f∥L2+∥curl f∥B∞,∞0n+∑j=n∞2j⁡(2−s)2j⁡(s−1)∥Δj∇f∥L2)\displaystyle c(\lVert f\rVert_{L^{2}}+\lVert\text{curl }f\rVert_{B_{\infty,\infty}^{0}}n+\sum_{j=n}^{\infty}2^{j(2-s)}2^{j(s-1)}\lVert\Delta_{j}\nabla f\rVert_{L^{2}})
≤\displaystyle\leq c⁡(∥f∥L2+∥curl ​f∥L∞​n+2n⁡(2−s)​∥f∥Hs)\displaystyle c(\lVert f\rVert_{L^{2}}+\lVert\text{curl }f\rVert_{L^{\infty}}n+2^{n(2-s)}\lVert f\rVert_{H^{s}})

by Young’s inequality for convolution, Bernstein’s inequalities and continuity of Riesz transform. Choosing n=(1s−2)​log2⁡(2+∥u∥Hs)n=\left(\frac{1}{s-2}\right)\log_{2}(2+\lVert u\rVert_{H^{s}}) immediately implies the desired result.
